1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.7.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.1808/2015 ON THE FILE OF THE 7TH ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, 32ND ACMM, MACT, BENGALURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the petitioner is seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 26.02.2015 at about 9.30 a.m., while the petitioner was riding the Bajaj Chetak Scooter bearing registration No.KA-05-ED-1540 as a pillion rider on Bengaluru-Kanakapura Road, near Sommanahalli KEB Gate, motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-05-EZ-9259 came and dashed against the Bajaj Chetak due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

After taking NC: 2024:KHC:32988 treatment at Government Hospital,
Kaggalipura and Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.6 Lakhs.
Claim was opposed by Respondent No.1.
After taking the evidence and hearing both the parties, the Tribunal by the impugned judgment, awarded global compensation of Rs.20,000/-.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Shri Sridhar.D.S., learned counsel for the petitioner and Shri S.Nagaraja,
learned counsel for Respondent No.1.
5.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered fracture of both the bones of left leg.
He was under hospitalization for forty days and has spent huge amount towards treatment and incidental expenses.
The Tribunal erroneously awarded global compensation for the reason that the owner of the motorcycle did not have the policy of insurance.
Per contra, learned counsel for the first respondent has contended that the Tribunal has awarded the compensation proportionate to the injuries.
There is contributory negligence on part of the petitioner, same was not considered by the Tribunal and supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.

2

8. The material on record goes to show that on 26.02.2015 at about 9.30 a.m., near Sommanahalli,
on Bengaluru-Kanakapura Road, there was an accident involving a Scooter, in which the petitioner was a pillion rider and a motorcycle, due to which, the petitioner has suffered injuries.

The medical record shows that the petitioner has suffered fracture of both the bones of left leg and was treated at Government Hospital, Kaggalipura and also at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru and he was hospitalized for forty days.
The Respondent No.1 though alleged the plea of contributory negligence, there is no evidence in support of it.
The Tribunal has rightly attributed negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and the petitioner being the victim is entitled to claim compensation.
There is no reason assigned by the Tribunal why global compensation is awarded.
The accident is of the year 2015, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.9,000/- per month.
Petitioner has spent money towards incidental expenses and suffered pain and sufferings and loss of amenities and discomforts.

Hence, in a case of this nature, compensation has to be assessed on different heads as hereunder:
 Sl. No. Particulars

Rs . 
 1 Pain and suffering 30,000/-
 2 Medical bills 5,000/-
 3 Loss of amenities and 20,000/-
 discomfort  4 Loss of income for two months 18,000/-
 during laid up period 9,000X2  5

Incidental expenses 10,000/-
 Total 83,000/-
Less: compensation 20,000/-
Awarded by the Tribunal

Enhanced compensation 63,000/-
 NC: 2024:KHC:32988 It is the just compensation that the petitioner would be entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:

Sd/-
